title: id: implement server-side identity backup per #5033 decision (v1 envelope blob, epoch-guarded storage, download budget)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

body:
## Problem
Issue #5033 recorded the design decision (2026-11-08, task 12716) for a server-side identity backup: the blob is the #2279 v1 envelope byte-for-byte, the server holds ciphertext + metadata only, OPRF is rejected for v1 in favour of a per-identity download budget over the pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs limiter shape plus the Argon2id guessing-cost floor, storage is one epoch-guarded record per identity with signed deletion, and restore-forces-rotation is deferred to the #2380 keyset substrate with an interim restore_epoch + device-notification rule. Nothing of this exists in code: at main 9f5a92057d pkgs/id has no backup record, endpoint, or lifecycle, and the identity key is still the raw file at pkgs/id/src/lib.rs:324.

## Implementation scope (from the #5033 decision)
- Server backup record keyed by hex(SHA-256(identity public key)) holding only: envelope bytes, envelope SHA-256, blob size, upload/download timestamps, monotone upload epoch, throttle counters, restore_epoch, and a deletion tombstone (H(pub) + final epoch).
- Upload endpoint: accepts envelope bytes + Sign_identity(H(pub) || envelope_sha256 || epoch); verifies the signature against the named public key; rejects non-increasing epochs; overwrites only on a valid higher-epoch upload.
- Download endpoint: requester presents the identity public key; server enforces the download budget (10/hour, 50/day per H(pub), weighted fixed windows per pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs, plus existing per-IP/global limits, refusals with retry-after) and returns the envelope bytes. Decryption stays client-side via the existing pkgs/id/src/key_envelope.rs import path; the passphrase never leaves the device.
- Delete endpoint: signed by the identity key; deletes ciphertext + counters, leaves the tombstone; account deletion purges the tombstone.
- Restore bookkeeping: a download-for-restore increments restore_epoch and notifies bound devices before the restored key is treated as authoritative for new group epochs (interim rule from #5033 item 5). Do NOT implement a rotation flag: that representation belongs to #2380 and lands there.
- Client: backup create/upload flow reusing key_envelope.rs encryption exactly (no second format), with a weak-passphrase warning at creation (per #5033 item 3's guessing-cost analysis).

## Acceptance
- [ ] A server data dump for a backup record contains no field beyond the #5033 item-2 list (test asserts the stored field set).
- [ ] Upload with a bad signature or a stale/equal epoch is rejected; a higher-epoch signed upload replaces the blob (tests naming their oracle: the #5033 decision items 1 and 4).
- [ ] The 11th download within an hour and the 51st within a day for one H(pub) are refused with retry-after (property test over the limiter: the budget invariant holds for arbitrary interleavings).
- [ ] Restore flow recovers the identity key from passphrase + downloaded envelope using only the existing key_envelope.rs decrypt path; wrong passphrase fails locally with no server signal.
- [ ] Signed delete removes the ciphertext; replaying the pre-delete signed upload does not resurrect it.
- [ ] No rotation flag is introduced; restore_epoch increment + bound-device notification are covered by tests.

## Out of scope
OPRF/blinded unwrap (rejected for v1 on #5033, revisit only as a v2 online assist), seed-phrase restore (#2381), guardian recovery (#2382), the restore-forces-rotation flag representation (#2380).

## Sources
Design decision on #5033 (comment 6718342769); investigation doc/2026-10-29T11-28-18Z_investigation_key_recovery_hosted sections 4.2, 7, 8.4; pkgs/id/src/key_envelope.rs; pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs.

## Acceptance criteria
- The v1 backup envelope format is documented in the implementation: version field, epoch semantics, and blob layout, matching the #5033 decision items 1-4.
- A server-side identity backup can be written and restored round-trip in tests, with epoch mismatch and malformed-blob cases refused with named errors.
- No client key material is logged or persisted outside the envelope; restore requires the documented epoch/credential checks.
- Tests named per the testing doctrine (invariant/oracle stated) cover round-trip, epoch roll, and corruption cases.
